titleEn: Acute Stroke - FAST-VAN and the Last-Seen-Normal Clock

patient.name: Linda Okafor
patient.affectEn: awake, frightened and tearful; sitting on a kitchen chair propped up by her husband; right side of the face drooping, drooling slightly; right arm hanging limp; follows every command and understands everything said around her
patient.speechEn: speech slurred and effortful (dysarthria) with some word-finding difficulty; can answer yes/no and give short words, so the husband supplies most of the history; never confused about who or where she is

scene.settingEn: Kitchen of a garden-suite home in Surrey at 1105 hrs. Warm, well lit. A dropped mug and spilled tea are on the floor beside the patient - a slip hazard. The patient sits on a kitchen chair, propped by her husband. Nothing suggests a fall or head strike. One patient.
hazardsEn: dropped mug and spilled tea on the kitchen floor - slip hazard

bystanders.knowsEn: She was completely normal at 1050, talking to him while she made tea; the mug fell from her right hand and her face changed within seconds (LAST SEEN NORMAL 1050, WITNESSED ONSET). He called 911 within minutes. No headache, no vomiting, no seizure, no fall, no head strike. Her symptoms have not improved. Two weeks ago she had a similar episode lasting 10 minutes that went away completely; she did not seek care. PMHx: atrial fibrillation, high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, previous TIA. Meds: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (last dose 0800 today), metoprolol, metformin, perindopril. No known allergies. Tea and toast at 0900; nothing since the onset. He answers only what he is asked.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
portable suction unit, OPA and NPA sets
ASA, oral glucose gel and nitroglycerin spray (in the drug kit)
PCP only: IV start kit with 18 G catheters, normal saline and administration set

dispatchEn: 1105 hrs. Code 3 to a garden-suite home in Surrey. 68-year-old female with sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech. Her husband called within minutes of onset. The nearest stroke-capable centre is 22 minutes away; the closest hospital without imaging is 8 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: onset was witnessed at about 1050 while she was making tea. She is awake but cannot lift her right arm.
arrivalEn: The husband meets you at the door and leads you to the kitchen. A dropped mug and spilled tea are on the floor. His wife sits on a kitchen chair and he is propping her up. The room is warm and well lit. One patient. Your partner is right behind you with the kits.
firstLookEn: A 68-year-old woman sitting on a kitchen chair, held upright by her husband. The right side of her face is drooping and she is drooling slightly. Her right arm hangs limp at her side. She is awake, looks at you, and is frightened and tearful.

primary.locEn: Alert. Eyes open spontaneously, follows commands, knows who and where she is; she understands everything but her speech is slurred and effortful with some word-finding difficulty. AVPU = A. (Dysarthria is a focal deficit, not a decreased LOC.)
primary.airwayEn: Patent, but she is drooling and has a weak swallow - aspiration risk. No foreign material, no vomit.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 18, regular, adequate depth, equal chest rise, no distress.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 88, irregularly irregular. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey for a medical patient: no trauma anywhere, no incontinence. Right-sided facial droop. Right arm and leg weak - she cannot hold the right arm up against gravity; grip absent on the right, normal on the left. Skin pink, warm, dry (skin is given automatically with the RBS). No fall and no head strike: c-spine is not indicated.

history.ccEn: Husband: "She suddenly couldn't use her right arm and her speech went slurred." Patient (slurred, effortful): "My arm... won't... work."

opqrst.oEn: Husband: "She was completely normal at 1050, talking to me while she made tea. The mug fell out of her right hand and her face changed within seconds." (Last seen normal 1050, witnessed onset.)
opqrst.pEn: Husband: "Nothing makes it better or worse. It hasn't improved at all since it started."
opqrst.qEn: Husband: "Her right arm and leg are weak, the right side of her face is drooping, her words are slurred and she's struggling to find words."
opqrst.rEn: Husband: "Two weeks ago she had something like this that lasted about 10 minutes and then went away completely. She didn't see anyone about it."
opqrst.sEn: Patient (shakes her head, slurred): "Can't... lift... my arm." Husband: "She can't lift her right arm at all."
opqrst.tEn: Husband: "It started at about 1050 and it hasn't changed since."

history.painScoreEn: No pain: she shakes her head - "No... no pain." No headache.

sample.sEn: Husband: "Weak right arm and leg, her face is drooping, slurred speech and some drooling. No headache, no vomiting, no seizure, she didn't fall and didn't hit her head."
sample.aEn: Husband: "No allergies that we know of." Patient shakes her head.
sample.mEn: Husband: "Apixaban 5 milligrams twice a day - she took this morning's dose at 0800 - plus metoprolol, metformin and perindopril."
sample.pEn: Husband: "Atrial fibrillation, high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and she's had a TIA before."
sample.lEn: Husband: "Tea and toast at 0900 this morning, and nothing since this started."
sample.eEn: Husband: "She was making tea and talking to me. Then the mug fell out of her right hand and her face changed. She didn't fall and she didn't hit her head."

fe.generalEn: (Yes/no answers, husband helps) Well until today.
fe.cnsEn: Right-sided weakness and numbness. No headache, no loss of vision, no seizure. One previous TIA two weeks ago.
fe.respiratoryEn: No, nothing - no shortness of breath, no cough.
fe.cardiovascularEn: Known atrial fibrillation; she takes a blood thinner (apixaban). No chest pain.
fe.giGuEn: No incontinence. Swallowing feels difficult. No vomiting.
fe.integumentaryEn: No, nothing - no rashes or sores.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: Right arm and leg are weak. No injuries.
fe.endocrineEn: Type 2 diabetes; her sugars are usually well controlled.
fe.eentEn: No double vision. No numbness on the left side of the face.

findings.headNeckEn: Right facial droop involving the lower face with forehead sparing. Tongue deviates to the right. No trauma to the head or neck. No neck stiffness.
findings.chestLungsEn: Clear and equal air entry at all 6 sites. Heart rhythm irregular.
findings.backEn: No findings: no tenderness, no deformity, no injury.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Right leg weak at 2 out of 5 versus 5 out of 5 on the left; sensation reduced on the right.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Right arm 1 out of 5 with no grip; left arm 5 out of 5. The right arm drifts and falls immediately when raised.
findings.fastVanEn: FAST-VAN, given element by element only as the candidate tests it: Face - right droop (positive); Arm - right arm drift (positive); Speech - slurred (positive); Time - last seen normal 1050; Vision - no visual field loss; Aphasia - mild word-finding difficulty; Neglect - none.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: en route, deficit unchanged (FAST-VAN unchanged, right arm still 1 out of 5)

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: Her speech has become unintelligible and she begins to vomit.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan glucometer, oxygen, stroke assessment tool, and a stretcher to the patient
Recognize this is a time-critical call where the last-seen-normal time and destination choice determine the outcome
triggers: we need the last seen normal time

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (spilled liquid and broken mug), environment, nature of illness (possible stroke), one patient
triggers: nature of illness is a possible stroke

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection
First look: right facial droop, drooling, right arm hanging limp, awake and frightened
Confirm with the husband whether she fell or struck her head before deciding on spinal precautions
triggers: how did she get to the chair

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert - and note that dysarthria is not a decreased LOC
triggers: speech is slurred but she's alert
do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: Verbalize c-spine not indicated after confirming no fall or head strike
Assess the airway and recognize the aspiration risk from drooling and a weak swallow - keep her NPO and have suction ready
Assess breathing
Assess circulation and note the irregularly irregular pulse (atrial fibrillation - a stroke risk factor)
Modified rapid body survey including a check for trauma and incontinence
Note skin: pink warm dry
Provide supplemental oxygen only to maintain SpO2 at or above 94 percent - at 96 percent none is required; verbalize the decision
triggers: SpO2 is 96 so no oxygen needed

expected.actionEn: Position with the head of the bed elevated and the affected side supported; protect the airway given the drooling
Categorize as RTC and act with urgency
Ready to load within 15 minutes - on-scene time is brain tissue
Choose the stroke-capable centre and verbalize the bypass rationale; notify the facility while en route
Establish chief complaint: sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech
HxC/C centred on the LAST SEEN NORMAL time and whether onset was witnessed, plus progression, headache, vomiting, seizure and previous TIA
triggers: when was she last seen normal

expected.actionEn: PMHx incl atrial fibrillation, diabetes, hypertension and previous TIA
Medications - especially anticoagulants and the exact time of the last dose
triggers: is she on a blood thinner

expected.actionEn: Allergies
LOI - relevant to both anesthesia planning and aspiration risk
GCS with components
BP by auscultation - document the hypertension; do NOT attempt to lower it
Pulse - identify the irregularly irregular rhythm
Respirations rate/depth/character
Skin hands-on
Pupils - required in a neurological presentation and repeated every set
SpO2 with calibration
triggers: check the waveform matches the pulse

expected.actionEn: BGL - explicitly required by the Stroke guideline to exclude hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic
Perform and document a formal FAST-VAN assessment for accurate recognition
FE - General health
FE - CNS (the core system here: weakness, numbness, vision, headache, previous TIA)
FE - Respiratory
FE - Cardiovascular (atrial fibrillation and anticoagulation)
FE - GI/GU (swallowing, incontinence)
FE - Integumentary
FE - Musculoskeletal
FE - Endocrine (diabetes)
FE - EENT (diplopia, facial sensation)
Head/neck exam incl facial symmetry, tongue deviation and trauma screen
Chest exam with 6-site auscultation
Abdomen exam
Back exam
Lower extremities with bilateral strength and sensory comparison documented
triggers: push against my hands with your feet

expected.actionEn: Upper extremities with bilateral grip strength and arm drift documented
Execute the Stroke protocol: ABCs, oxygen to target, positioning, BGL, FAST-VAN, timely transport with notification
Establish and document the last-seen-normal time precisely - it determines thrombolysis and thrombectomy eligibility
Keep the patient NPO and have suction available given the drooling and weak swallow
PCP: vascular access en route with an 18 G above the wrist, preferably on the right
triggers: start a line in the truck

expected.actionEn: Do not give ASA, oral glucose, or anything by mouth in a suspected stroke with a swallowing deficit
Reassess ABCs and interventions after each move and each change in presentation
Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes plus a repeat neurological assessment
Manage any vomiting immediately with suction and positioning without compromising the airway
Continue to protect the affected limbs and reassure a frightened patient who can hear and understand everything
triggers: we're taking good care of you
I know you can hear me

expected.actionEn: Early en-route stroke-team notification stating the last-seen-normal time
Complete hand-off leading with last-seen-normal, FAST-VAN findings, BGL and anticoagulant use with the time of the last dose
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate asks for or states the last-seen-normal / onset time (e.g. 'when was she last seen normal?', 'what time did this start?', 'last known well 1050')
candidate decides to transport to the closer hospital without imaging (8 minutes away) instead of the stroke-capable centre (22 minutes away)
candidate gives her anything by mouth - food, a drink, water, tablets, ASA or oral glucose - despite the weak swallow (log drug:asa or drug:oral-glucose as well when those are given)
after the examiner says she is vomiting, the candidate does not suction and reposition her (e.g. onto her side) but carries on with other tasks
candidate applies manual c-spine control, a cervical collar or spinal motion restriction although there was no fall and no head strike
candidate inserts an OPA or NPA in this alert patient (treating the dysarthria as a decreased LOC)
candidate assists or provides ventilations with a BVM although she is alert and breathing adequately at 18
candidate applies high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather while SpO2 is 96% on room air without a titration rationale
candidate lets or asks her to stand up or walk (e.g. to the stretcher or out of the house) despite the right-sided weakness

candidate delays leaving the scene to complete the full head-to-toe examination of every body region, the functional enquiry or the IV before moving her to the cot or loading (a focused FAST-VAN, grip and arm-drift check on scene is correct and is NOT this event)
PCP gives a fluid bolus (e.g. 20 mL/kg or runs the saline wide open) although her blood pressure is high

drugs.doseEn: WITHHELD in this call: ASA (160 mg PO) is indicated in the BC guidelines only for chest pain / symptoms consistent with cardiac ischemia - not for a suspected stroke; she also cannot swallow safely and takes apixaban (anticoagulant caution). If given, report drug:asa.

WITHHELD in this call: BGL is 8.9 mmol/L (not hypoglycemic) and she has a weak swallow; oral glucose (15 g) is only for a hypoglycemic patient with sufficient mentation to maintain an airway. If given, report drug:oral-glucose.

WITHHELD in this call: the indication is chest discomfort that appears cardiac (0.4 mg SL); she has no chest pain, and the hypertension of a suspected stroke is not treated pre-hospitally. If given, report drug:nitroglycerin.
PCP, en route: vascular access with an 18 G above the level of the wrist, preferably on the right side; saline lock or keep-vein-open only - no fluid bolus is indicated with this blood pressure.

notificationFacts.hxcc: witnessed onset, last seen normal 1050 while making tea; no headache, vomiting, seizure or fall; similar 10-minute episode two weeks ago that resolved; on apixaban, last dose 0800 today
notificationFacts.vitals: GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6), BP 186/104, pulse 88 irregularly irregular, resp 18, SpO2 96% on room air, BGL 8.9; latest BP 178/98, pulse 92, deficit unchanged
notificationFacts.treatments: ABCs managed, suction available, kept NPO, head elevated with the right side supported, oxygen not required at 96%; PCP: IV 18 G right forearm; bypassing the closer hospital to the stroke-capable centre, ETA 22 minutes
notificationFacts.findings: FAST-VAN positive: right facial droop, right arm drift (1 out of 5, no grip), right leg 2 out of 5, slurred speech with mild word-finding difficulty, no visual field loss, no neglect

handoffFacts.cc: sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech, suspected acute stroke
handoffFacts.hxcc: witnessed onset - LAST SEEN NORMAL 1050 while making tea, about 35 minutes from onset at hand-off; the mug fell from her right hand and her face changed within seconds; no headache, vomiting, seizure, fall or head strike; no improvement; a similar 10-minute episode two weeks ago resolved and was not reported
handoffFacts.initialVitals: GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6), BP 186/104, pulse 88 irregularly irregular, resp 18 regular, skin pink warm dry, pupils equal and reactive 3 mm, SpO2 96% on room air, BGL 8.9 mmol/L, temperature 36.8
handoffFacts.finalVitals: GCS 14, BP 178/98, pulse 92 irregularly irregular, resp 18, skin pink warm dry, pupils equal and reactive 3 mm, SpO2 96% on room air, BGL 8.9; FAST-VAN unchanged, right arm still 1 out of 5
handoffFacts.pmhx: atrial fibrillation, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, previous TIA (the episode two weeks ago)
handoffFacts.meds: apixaban 5 mg twice daily - LAST DOSE 0800 TODAY; metoprolol, metformin, perindopril
handoffFacts.treatments: airway monitored with suction available; kept nil by mouth for a weak swallow; head elevated with the right side supported; oxygen not required (SpO2 96%); BGL checked (8.9) to exclude a hypoglycemic mimic; FAST-VAN performed; PCP: IV 18 G in the right forearm; bypassed the local hospital to the stroke-capable centre with pre-notification
handoffFacts.findings: right lower facial droop with forehead sparing, tongue deviates right; right arm 1 out of 5 with no grip and immediate drift, left 5 out of 5; right leg 2 out of 5 with reduced sensation, left 5 out of 5; dysarthria with mild word-finding difficulty; no visual field loss, no neglect; chest clear, irregular rhythm

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR performs the entire Stroke guideline: ABCs, oxygen titrated to 94 percent or above, positioning, blood glucose check, FAST-VAN recognition, NPO, timely transport and notification. EMR does not establish vascular access. No Functional Enquiry. EMR must not give ASA for a stroke - ASA in the BC guidelines is for cardiac chest pain, not CVA.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds en-route vascular access with an 18 gauge above the wrist, preferably on the right side so the left is free for imaging and intervention, plus the 9-system Functional Enquiry adapted to her speech deficit (yes/no questions, husband helps). No fluid bolus is indicated, and the hypertension must not be treated pre-hospitally.

sourcePages: Scenario md-06 (data/practical/scenarios.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport (bypass to the stroke-capable centre), history (last seen normal 1050, apixaban last dose 0800), vitals sets 1-2 and FAST-VAN, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing (examiner option: unintelligible speech and vomiting if not reassessing), handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (suspected CVA, new onset neurological deficits = unstable); p.11 Primary Survey interventions (c-spine only with an indication; oxygen indications); p.13 AVPU (alert); p.30 Stroke (ABCs, SpO2 >= 94%, position, blood glucose check, FAST-VAN, timely transport and en-route notification; PCP en-route vascular access 18 G above the wrist, preferably on the right); p.60 Aspirin (indication: chest pain / cardiac ischemia; contraindication inability to swallow; caution anticoagulants); p.73 Nitroglycerin (indication: cardiac chest discomfort); p.76 Oral Glucose (only with sufficient mentation to maintain an airway).
